## Findings
- claim-1: For \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), \(J_v\subset H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) is generated as an ideal by \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}\). [source-2@L1382-L1401|claim=formal-document]
- claim-2: Under the recorded integral graded presentation hypotheses and the accepted degreewise certificates, if \(a=1,b=2\), then \(Q=J_v/A_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^3\).
## Strategy
Assume the recorded integral graded box/Schur/Pieri presentation of \(A\), \(J_v\), and \(Q=J_v/A_+J_v\). Put \(d=ij\). For \(a=1,b=2\), source-backed ideal generation gives
\[
J_v=(x_0,x_1,x_2),\qquad
x_0=s_{i^j},\quad x_1=s_{(i+1,i^{j-1})},\quad
x_2=s_{((i+1)^2,i^{j-2})}.
\]
Since \(A/A_+\cong\mathbb Z\), reduction modulo \(A_+J_v\) yields the graded surjection
\[
\phi:\mathbb Zx_0\oplus\mathbb Zx_1\oplus\mathbb Zx_2\twoheadrightarrow Q.
\]

The source has respective degrees \(d,d+1,d+2\). Here
\[
p=q-i,\quad c=r-j,\qquad \min(p,c)=a=1.
\]
The accepted degreewise certificates cover \(p=1,c\ge2\), \(c=1,p\ge2\), and \(p=c=1\), and establish integrally
\[
Q_d=\mathbb Z\bar x_0,\qquad
Q_{d+1}=\mathbb Z\bar x_1,\qquad
Q_{d+2}=\mathbb Z\bar x_2.
\]
Thus each homogeneous component of \(\phi\) on its support is an isomorphism. Since the source has no other homogeneous components, its homogeneous kernel vanishes in every degree, hence \(\ker\phi=0\). Therefore
\[
Q\cong\mathbb Z\bar x_0\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_1\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_2\cong\mathbb Z^3.
\]

The requested standalone graded-kernel globalization certificate is established, conditional on the recorded presentation hypotheses and accepted degreewise certificates.

## Gaps
The conclusion remains conditional on the integral box/Schur/Pieri presentation and the accepted low-degree certificates. No assertion of minimality or any broader parent theorem is made.
